# appgatesdp_appliance_controller_activation (Resource)

Enables or disables the controller function of an activated appliance and waits until the appliance reaches the matching state (controller_ready or appliance_ready). The `controller` and `admin_interface` attributes are those of `appgatesdp_appliance`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Turns an activated appliance into an additional controller and waits until
# it reports controller_ready. Destroying it disables the controller function.
resource "appgatesdp_appliance_controller_activation" "second" {
  appliance_id = appgatesdp_appliance.controller_2.id
  wait_timeout = "30m"

  controller = {
    enabled = true
  }

  admin_interface = {
    hostname      = "controller-2.example.com"
    https_ciphers = ["ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384", "ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256"]
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `admin_interface` (Attributes) The details of the admin connection interface. Required on Controllers and LogServers. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--admin_interface))
- `appliance_id` (String) ID of an activated appliance.
- `controller` (Attributes) Controller settings. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--controller))

### Optional

- `wait_timeout` (String) How long to wait for the appliance to reach its target state, as a duration. Defaults to `45m`. If it is exceeded, the apply succeeds with a warning.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) ID of the appliance.

<a id="nestedatt--admin_interface"></a>
### Nested Schema for `admin_interface`

Optional:

- `allow_sources` (Attributes List) Source configuration to allow via iptables. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--admin_interface--allow_sources))
- `hostname` (String) Hostname to connect to the admin interface. This hostname will be used to validate the appliance certificate. Set it to "automatic.hostname.assignment" for cloud appliances in order for it to automatically configure the hostname on activation.
- `https_ciphers` (List of String) The type of TLS ciphers to allow. See: https://www.openssl.org/docs/man1.0.2/apps/ciphers.html for all supported ciphers.
- `https_p12` (Attributes) PKCS12 object with X.509 certificate and private key. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--admin_interface--https_p12))
- `https_port` (Number) Port to connect for admin services.
- `https_signed_certificate_pem` (String, Sensitive) A PEM-encoded signed certificate to complete a pending CSR flow. Provide this field when submitting the CA-signed certificate obtained after generating a CSR. Requires a pending CSR key pair (generated via POST /appliances/{id}/admin-interface/csr). The certificate must match the public key from the CSR and cover the appliance hostname. Supported in API versions: v25.

Read-Only:

- `https_certificate_type` (String) Indicates how the admin interface HTTPS certificate is currently configured. Supported in API versions: v25.

<a id="nestedatt--admin_interface--allow_sources"></a>
### Nested Schema for `admin_interface.allow_sources`

Optional:

- `address` (String) IP address to allow connection.
- `netmask` (Number) Netmask to use with address for allowing connections.
- `nic` (String) NIC name to accept connections on.


<a id="nestedatt--admin_interface--https_p12"></a>
### Nested Schema for `admin_interface.https_p12`

Optional:

- `content` (String) Contents of the P12 file in Base64 format.
- `id` (String) Identifier to track the object on update since all the other fields are write-only. A random one will be assigned if left empty.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Password for the P12 file.

Read-Only:

- `subject_name` (String) Subject name of the certificate in the file.



<a id="nestedatt--controller"></a>
### Nested Schema for `controller`

Optional:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the Controller is enabled on this appliance or not. Cannot be enabled on an inactive Appliance since some checks need to be done first.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Imported by appliance ID.
terraform import appgatesdp_appliance_controller_activation.second 4c07bc67-57ea-42dd-b702-c2d6c45419fc
```
